decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 6.5%.

changes.quote: The drag on demand and profits from rising energy costs, as well as eroding consumer confidence, reports of substantial shortfalls in sales and earnings, and stress in some segments of the financial markets suggest that economic growth may be slowing further.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: While some inflation risks persist, they are diminished by the more moderate pace of economic activity and by the absence of any indication that longer-term inflation expectations have increased.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The Committee will continue to monitor closely the evolving economic situation.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee, accordingly, continues to see a risk of heightened inflation pressures.”

changes.quote: Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee consequently believes that the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The utilization of the pool of available workers remains at an unusually high level, and the increase in energy prices, though having limited effect on core measures of prices to date, still harbors the possibility of raising inflation expectations.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: However, softening in business and household demand and tightening conditions in financial markets over recent months suggest that the economy could expand for a time at a pace below the productivity-enhanced rate of growth of its potential to produce.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: Against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the Committee consequently believes that the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.

The drag on demand and profits from rising energy costs, as well as eroding consumer confidence, reports of substantial shortfalls in sales and earnings, and stress in some segments of the financial markets suggest that economic growth may be slowing further.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 15.98% APR costs about $66.58 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.19% and moved +2 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.54% would rise by about $4.12 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 107k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.4% over the past year (November 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates).

citations.detail: The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to maintain the existing stance of monetary policy, keeping its target for the federal funds rate at 6-1/2 percent.
